newsitem.title: UK: LCE coffee ends weaker after arbitrage selling.
newsitem.headline: LCE coffee ends weaker after arbitrage selling.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures closed weaker across the board on Thursday after a wave of arbitrage trade selling against the arabicas market, but some managed to steer clear of earlier lows, traders said.

"It (London) is doing pretty well against New York, the arbs are coming in," said one trader. At the close the key November contract stood down $25 at $1,520, just above a session low of $1,518. Other traded positions were around $23-$24 weaker in total market volume of 5,376 lots, over half of which was in November.
Earlier, traders cited keen origin selling from Asia and possibly Africa, but trade players stepped in after New York opened to sell robusta positions against New York.
"It's probably more trade (sellers), I haven't heard of any particular origin selling," said another trader.
"There's nothing fundamentally around, the market's holding well..it's not doing too badly," he said. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 8064
